scheme_name: Disha - Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme
description:
The Disha - Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme was launched by the Government of India on 1st April 2021. 

This scheme is specifically designed to address the needs of children aged 0 to 6 years who are at risk of developmental delays. 

The initiative aims to provide early intervention services to enhance the cognitive, physical, and emotional development of these children. 

The primary objective of the Disha scheme is to ensure that children with developmental delays are identified early and provided with the necessary support. 

The scheme aims to achieve a target of reaching at least 1 million children annually within the first three years of its implementation. 

Disha also focuses on improving school readiness among children aged 3 to 6 years. 

The initiative seeks to equip children with the necessary skills to transition smoothly into formal schooling. 

The benefits of the Disha scheme include access to early intervention services such as developmental assessments, therapy, and educational support. 

Families of eligible children can receive financial assistance of up to INR 5,000 per month for a maximum period of 12 months. 

This financial support is aimed at alleviating the economic burden on families while they seek necessary interventions for their children. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme provides access to specialized services such as speech therapy, occupational therapy, and psychological counseling. 

Eligibility criteria for the Disha scheme include children aged between 0 to 6 years who are identified as having developmental delays or disabilities. 

Parents or guardians must provide a medical certificate from a recognized healthcare professional to confirm the child's condition. 

Income criteria stipulate that families must have an annual income of less than INR 3 lakhs to qualify for the financial assistance component. 

The application process for the Disha scheme involves several steps. 

First, parents or guardians must visit the nearest Anganwadi center or local health facility to obtain information about the scheme. 

They will need to fill out an application form that includes details about the child's health and developmental history. 

Required documents include a copy of the child's birth certificate, proof of income, and the medical certificate confirming the developmental delay. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by a panel of experts who will conduct a developmental assessment of the child. 

The assessment will determine the level of intervention required and the specific services that will be provided. 

Families will be notified of the outcome of the assessment within 30 days of submission. 

If approved, families will begin receiving financial assistance within 15 days of the approval notification. 

The Disha scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development in collaboration with state governments. 

Each state has designated nodal officers responsible for overseeing the implementation of the scheme at the local level. 

Contact details for state nodal officers can typically be found on the official website of the Ministry of Women and Child Development. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to improve early childhood care and education across India. 

It aligns with the National Policy for Children 2013, which emphasizes the importance of early intervention for children with developmental challenges. 

The Disha scheme is also linked to the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) program, which aims to provide comprehensive health and nutrition services to children. 

Statistical data indicates that approximately 10% of children in India may experience some form of developmental delay. 

This highlights the critical need for early intervention services to support these children and their families. 

The Disha scheme is expected to significantly reduce the number of children who enter school unprepared. 

Research shows that early intervention can lead to improved educational outcomes and better quality of life for children with developmental delays. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of parental involvement in the early intervention process. 

Parents are encouraged to participate in training sessions that provide guidance on supporting their child's development at home. 

These sessions cover topics such as effective communication strategies and developmental milestones. 

The Disha scheme also promotes awareness about developmental delays among healthcare providers and educators. 

Workshops and training programs are organized to equip professionals with the skills needed to identify and support children at risk. 

The government aims to create a network of support services that are accessible to families across urban and rural areas. 

Monitoring and evaluation mechanisms are in place to assess the effectiveness of the Disha scheme. 

Data will be collected on the number of children served, the types of interventions provided, and the outcomes achieved. 

This information will be used to refine and improve the scheme over time. 

The Disha scheme represents a significant investment in the future of India's children. 

By focusing on early intervention and school readiness, the government aims to create a more inclusive and equitable education system. 

The scheme is expected to contribute to the overall development of children and reduce the long-term impact of developmental delays. 

In conclusion, the Disha - Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme is a comprehensive initiative aimed at supporting children with developmental delays. 

With specific financial assistance, targeted interventions, and a focus on parental involvement, the scheme seeks to ensure that every child has the opportunity to thrive. 

Families are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme to secure the best possible start for their children. 

For more information, families can visit the official website of the Ministry of Women and Child Development or contact their local Anganwadi center. 

The Disha scheme is a vital step towards building a brighter future for children with developmental challenges in India.
